--- external deployment documentation ---
unsynchronized without excluding vault content. Visual Studio Code requests a
native title bar, disables its bundled
AI/Copilot features, and applies the managed built-in dark workbench, terminal,
syntax, semantic-token, privacy, and editor UX defaults. The shared Labwc
environment requests compositor
decorations from Qt and GTK with
`QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION=1` and `GTK_CSD=0`. Filen has no supported
native-frame preference and hardcodes its own renderer controls, so the
config-only contract can disable Chromium's decoration fallback but cannot
remove Filen's embedded controls without changing the vendor application. The
desktop role does not add this class automatically; select it explicitly when
you want the monolithic external software bundle instead of the per-app
`apps/*` classes.

Before `pkgsel`, the shared installer hooks temporarily divert the target's real
`/usr/bin/unshare` and replace it with a success-only shim. This covers package
maintainer scripts and the later direct vendor Debian transactions that probe
user namespaces from the restricted d-i environment. The final
`99-normalize-finish` hook validates the installer marker, removes the shim, and
restores the diverted real binary before the installed system boots. The six
direct vendor Debian transactions and the scheduled managed external-software
updater keep `NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1` scoped to their automatic package
transactions, so they never request restart handling for services or user
sessions. Administrator-initiated APT operations and every application or
Bubblewrap sandbox use the real `unshare(1)` binary.
Installer downloads are confined to `/tmp/installer-software` and removed on
success, failure, or interruption; the managed post-boot updater likewise uses
a private `/tmp/managed-external-software-update.*` workspace. Managed
application payloads use a non-brittle 1 MiB transport floor; Debian archives
are still required to pass archive framing, metadata, architecture, executable,
and desktop-entry validation, while Tuta remains protected by its pinned
signature and executable AppImage checks.
The verified Ledger AppImage is extracted into root-owned `/opt/ledger-live`,
its bundled Chromium sandbox is the only payload granted setuid-root mode, and
the managed launcher keeps native Wayland plus KWallet-backed password storage
without the vendor desktop file's `--no-sandbox` argument. A class-scoped udev
rule covers Ledger Stax and other current `2c97` devices, including
re-enumerated firmware-update modes, while keeping USB and hidraw nodes at
`0660` with `plugdev` plus active-seat `uaccess`; the vendor rule's
world-writable `0666` hidraw mode is not used.

Selecting `addon/software` also stages
`managed-external-software-update.timer`, which runs once each Sunday with a
bounded randomized delay and catches up after downtime. Its root oneshot
service downloads and revalidates the Bitwarden, Obsidian, Zoom, Filen, and
Discord Debian packages, compares their package versions with `dpkg`, rejects
downgrades, and installs only newer versions through APT. Ledger and Tuta
remain vendor-supported signed AppImage paths, so their verified hashes are
compared with recorded installed artifacts before atomic replacement. Obsidian
updates resolve the official latest stable GitHub release metadata, require one
version-matched amd64 Debian asset, and verify GitHub's asset SHA-256 digest and
declared size before the normal package and payload checks. Every verified
vendor Debian package is retained under
`/var/lib/managed-external-software/debs` and indexed as a root-owned local APT
repository. That gives ordinary APT transactions an archive from which to
recover an interrupted managed-package installation rather than leaving a
`reinstreq` package to block unrelated operations. Before network checks, the
updater also attempts an offline reinstall from that retained archive; if a
managed package remains unrecoverable, it removes only that broken package so
the rest of APT remains usable. Update lifecycle events are written to a
root-owned queue and delivered by class-scoped systemd user units through
`notify-send` to Mako, including checks, active updates, successful updates,
failures, and the final summary. Events created while no Labwc session is active
are replayed the next time that user's `labwc-session.target` starts.

`ssh.cfg` installs the target OpenSSH server package and enables the
shared late-command SSH configuration/key staging path when selected as
`classes=...,ssh`.

`wifi.cfg` is now only a compatibility marker that keeps Wi-Fi firmware loading

--- external updater: ledger metadata and Debian repository/recovery ---
parse_ledger_metadata() {
  metadata_path=$1

  [ "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^version: ' "$metadata_path")" -eq 1 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata must contain exactly one version"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^path: ' "$metadata_path")" -eq 1 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata must contain exactly one release path"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^sha512: ' "$metadata_path")" -eq 1 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata must contain exactly one release SHA-512"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$(/usr/bin/grep -c '^    size: ' "$metadata_path")" -eq 1 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata must contain exactly one release size"
    return 1
  }

  LEDGER_VERSION=$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/^version: //p' "$metadata_path")
  LEDGER_FILENAME=$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/^path: //p' "$metadata_path")
  LEDGER_METADATA_SHA512=$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/^sha512: //p' "$metadata_path")
  LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE=$(/usr/bin/sed -n 's/^    size: //p' "$metadata_path")

  case "$LEDGER_VERSION" in
    ''|.*|*.|*..*|*[!0123456789.]*)
      log_message error "Ledger release metadata has an invalid version: ${LEDGER_VERSION:-unset}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  [ "${#LEDGER_VERSION}" -le 32 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata version is too long"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$LEDGER_FILENAME" = "ledger-live-desktop-${LEDGER_VERSION}-linux-x86_64.AppImage" ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata has an unexpected AppImage path: ${LEDGER_FILENAME:-unset}"
    return 1
  }
  case "$LEDGER_METADATA_SHA512" in
    ''|*[!ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/=]*)
      log_message error "Ledger release metadata SHA-512 is invalid"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  [ "${#LEDGER_METADATA_SHA512}" -eq 88 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata SHA-512 has an unexpected length"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_metadata_digest_bytes=$(
    printf '%s' "$LEDGER_METADATA_SHA512" |
      /usr/bin/openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null |
      /usr/bin/wc -c |
      /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
  )
  [ "$ledger_metadata_digest_bytes" = 64 ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata SHA-512 does not decode to 64 bytes"
    return 1
  }
  case "$LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*)
      log_message error "Ledger release metadata size is invalid"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  if [ "$LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE" -lt 104857600 ] || [ "$LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE" -gt 536870912 ]; then
    log_message error "Ledger release metadata size is outside the approved range: $LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE"
    return 1
  fi
}

ledger_signed_sha512() {
  checksums_path=$1

  /usr/bin/awk -v wanted="$LEDGER_FILENAME" '
    $2 == wanted {
      count += 1
      hash = $1
    }
    END {
      if (count != 1 || length(hash) != 128 || hash !~ /^[0-9a-f]+$/) {
        exit 1
      }
      print hash
    }
  ' "$checksums_path"
}

deb_contains_path() {
  deb_path=$1
  expected_path=$2

  /usr/bin/dpkg-deb -c "$deb_path" 2>/dev/null |
    /usr/bin/awk -v wanted=".${expected_path}" '
      $6 == wanted { found = 1 }
      END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }
    '
}

validate_deb_artifact() {
  label=$1
  deb_path=$2
  expected_packages=$3
  expected_architecture=$4
  expected_executable=$5
  expected_desktop_file=$6
  expected_runtime_library=${7:-}

  validate_abs_path "$label package path" "$deb_path"
  validate_abs_path "$label executable path" "$expected_executable"
  validate_abs_path "$label desktop file path" "$expected_desktop_file"
  if [ -n "$expected_runtime_library" ]; then
    validate_abs_path "$label runtime library path" "$expected_runtime_library"
  fi
  [ -n "$expected_packages" ] || {
    log_message error "$label expected package names are empty"
    return 1
  }

  deb_magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 8 "$deb_path" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ "$deb_magic" = '!<arch>' ] || {
    log_message error "$label download does not have Debian archive framing"
    return 1
  }
  /usr/bin/dpkg-deb --info "$deb_path" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "$label download is not a valid Debian binary package"
    return 1
  }
  deb_contains_path "$deb_path" "$expected_executable" || {
    log_message error "$label package payload is missing executable: $expected_executable"
    return 1
  }
  deb_contains_path "$deb_path" "$expected_desktop_file" || {
    log_message error "$label package payload is missing desktop entry: $expected_desktop_file"
    return 1
  }
  if [ -n "$expected_runtime_library" ] &&
     ! deb_contains_path "$deb_path" "$expected_runtime_library"
  then
    log_message error "$label package payload is missing runtime library: $expected_runtime_library"
    return 1
  fi

  REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$deb_path" Package 2>/dev/null || true)
  REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$deb_path" Version 2>/dev/null || true)
  package_architecture=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$deb_path" Architecture 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" in
    ''|*[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+.-]*)
      log_message error "$label package has an invalid Package field: ${REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME:-unset}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  package_name_is_expected=false
  for expected_package in $expected_packages; do
    case "$expected_package" in
      ''|*[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+.-]*)
        log_message error "$label expected package name is invalid: ${expected_package:-unset}"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    if [ "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" = "$expected_package" ]; then
      package_name_is_expected=true
    fi
  done
  if [ "$package_name_is_expected" != true ]; then
    log_message error "$label package has an unexpected Package field: $REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME"
    return 1
  fi
  unset expected_package package_name_is_expected
  /usr/bin/dpkg --validate-version "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "$label package has an invalid Version field: ${REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION:-unset}"
    return 1
  }
  [ "${#REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION}" -le 128 ] || {
    log_message error "$label package Version field exceeds 128 characters"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$package_architecture" = "$expected_architecture" ] || {
    log_message error "$label package has an unexpected architecture: ${package_architecture:-unset}"
    return 1
  }
}

installed_package_version() {
  package_name=$1
  package_status=$(
    /usr/bin/dpkg-query \
      -W \
      -f='${Status}' \
      "$package_name" 2>/dev/null || true
  )
  [ "$package_status" = "install ok installed" ] || return 1

  package_version=$(
    /usr/bin/dpkg-query \
      -W \
      -f='${Version}\n' \
      "$package_name" 2>/dev/null || true
  )
  /usr/bin/dpkg --validate-version "$package_version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  [ "${#package_version}" -le 128 ] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$package_version"
}

installed_package_status() {
  package_name=$1

  /usr/bin/dpkg-query \
    -W \
    -f='${Status}' \
    "$package_name" 2>/dev/null || true
}

validate_deb_archive_component() {
  label=$1
  value=$2

  [ "${#value}" -le 128 ] || {
    log_message error "$label exceeds 128 characters"
    return 1
  }
  case "$value" in
    ''|*[!ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789.+:~_-]*)
      log_message error "$label contains unsupported archive-path characters: ${value:-unset}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

managed_deb_archive_path() {
  package_name=$1
  package_version=$2
  package_architecture=$3

  validate_deb_archive_component "managed package name" "$package_name" || return 1
  validate_deb_archive_component "managed package version" "$package_version" || return 1
  /usr/bin/dpkg --validate-version "$package_version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "managed package version is invalid: ${package_version:-unset}"
    return 1
  }
  [ "$package_architecture" = amd64 ] || {
    log_message error "managed package archive has unsupported architecture: ${package_architecture:-unset}"
    return 1
  }

  printf '%s/%s_%s_%s.deb\n' \
    "$DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR" \
    "$package_name" \
    "$package_version" \
    "$package_architecture"
}

managed_deb_repository_codename() {
  repository_codename=$(
    /usr/bin/awk -F= \
      '$1 == "VERSION_CODENAME" { print $2; exit }' \
      /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null || true
  )
  case "$repository_codename" in
    \"*\")
      repository_codename=${repository_codename#\"}
      repository_codename=${repository_codename%\"}
      ;;
  esac
  validate_deb_archive_component \
    "managed package repository codename" \
    "$repository_codename" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$repository_codename"
}

write_managed_deb_repository_source() {
  source_dir=$(/usr/bin/dirname "$DEB_REPOSITORY_SOURCE")
  source_tmp="${DEB_REPOSITORY_SOURCE}.tmp.$$"

  validate_abs_path "managed package repository source" "$DEB_REPOSITORY_SOURCE"
  [ ! -L "$DEB_REPOSITORY_SOURCE" ] || {
    log_message error "managed package repository source must not be a symlink"
    return 1
  }
  /usr/bin/install -d -m 0755 "$source_dir" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' \
    '# Managed by unattended-installer.' \
    '# Retained, validated vendor packages let APT repair managed applications' \
    '# without relying on a transient download directory.' \
    'deb [trusted=yes] file:/var/lib/managed-external-software/debs ./' >"$source_tmp"
  /bin/chmod 0644 "$source_tmp"
  /bin/mv -f -- "$source_tmp" "$DEB_REPOSITORY_SOURCE"
}

write_managed_deb_repository() {
  packages_tmp="${DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR}/.Packages.$$"
  packages_path="${DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR}/Packages"
  archive_count=0

  /usr/bin/install -d -m 0755 "$DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR" || return 1
  : >"$packages_tmp"
  /bin/chmod 0644 "$packages_tmp"

  for archive_path in "$DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR"/*.deb; do
    [ -f "$archive_path" ] && [ ! -L "$archive_path" ] || continue
    archive_name=${archive_path##*/}
    case "$archive_name" in
      *[!ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789.+:~_-]*)
        rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
        log_message error "managed package repository contains an unsafe archive name: $archive_name"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac

    archive_package=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$archive_path" Package 2>/dev/null || true)
    archive_version=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$archive_path" Version 2>/dev/null || true)
    archive_architecture=$(/usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$archive_path" Architecture 2>/dev/null || true)
    validate_deb_archive_component "managed repository package name" "$archive_package" || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      return 1
    }
    validate_deb_archive_component "managed repository package version" "$archive_version" || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      return 1
    }
    /usr/bin/dpkg --validate-version "$archive_version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      log_message error "managed repository package version is invalid: ${archive_version:-unset}"
      return 1
    }
    [ "$archive_architecture" = amd64 ] || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      log_message error "managed repository package has unsupported architecture: ${archive_architecture:-unset}"
      return 1
    }
    [ "$archive_name" = "${archive_package}_${archive_version}_${archive_architecture}.deb" ] || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      log_message error "managed repository archive name does not match its Debian control fields: $archive_name"
      return 1
    }
    /usr/bin/dpkg-deb -f "$archive_path" >>"$packages_tmp" || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      log_message error "unable to read managed package control metadata: $archive_name"
      return 1
    }
    archive_size=$(/usr/bin/wc -c <"$archive_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
    archive_sha256=$(/usr/bin/sha256sum "$archive_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
    case "$archive_size:$archive_sha256" in
      *[!0123456789abcdef:]*|:|*:)
        rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
        log_message error "managed package repository archive metadata is invalid: $archive_name"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    [ "${#archive_sha256}" -eq 64 ] || {
      rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
      log_message error "managed package repository archive SHA-256 has an unexpected length: $archive_name"
      return 1
    }
    printf 'Filename: ./%s\nSize: %s\nSHA256: %s\n\n' \
      "$archive_name" \
      "$archive_size" \
      "$archive_sha256" >>"$packages_tmp"
    archive_count=$((archive_count + 1))
  done

  [ "$archive_count" -gt 0 ] || {
    rm -f -- "$packages_tmp"
    return 1
  }
  /bin/mv -f -- "$packages_tmp" "$packages_path"

  repository_codename=$(managed_deb_repository_codename) || return 1
  repository_release_tmp="${DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR}/.Release.$$"
  repository_packages_size=$(/usr/bin/wc -c <"$packages_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
  repository_packages_sha256=$(/usr/bin/sha256sum "$packages_path" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
  repository_release_date=$(/usr/bin/date -Ru)
  case "$repository_packages_size:$repository_packages_sha256" in
    *[!0123456789abcdef:]*|:|*:)
      log_message error "managed package repository Packages metadata is invalid"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  [ "${#repository_packages_sha256}" -eq 64 ] || {
    log_message error "managed package repository Packages SHA-256 has an unexpected length"
    return 1
  }
  printf '%s\n' \
    'Origin: Managed External Software' \
    'Label: Managed External Software' \
    "Suite: ${repository_codename}" \
    "Codename: ${repository_codename}" \
    'Architectures: amd64' \
    "Date: ${repository_release_date}" \
    'SHA256:' \
    " ${repository_packages_sha256} ${repository_packages_size} Packages" \
    'Description: Retained validated vendor Debian packages' >"$repository_release_tmp"
  /bin/chmod 0644 "$repository_release_tmp"
  /bin/mv -f -- "$repository_release_tmp" "$DEB_REPOSITORY_RELEASE"
}

refresh_managed_deb_repository() {
  write_managed_deb_repository_source || return 1
  write_managed_deb_repository || return 1

  /usr/bin/env -i \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    HOME=/root \
    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 \
    NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1 \
    PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \
    /usr/bin/apt-get \
      -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist="sources.list.d/managed-external-software.list" \
      -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts="-" \
      -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=false \
      update
}

store_managed_deb_archive() {
  label=$1
  deb_path=$2
  archive_path=$(managed_deb_archive_path \
    "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" \
    "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" \
    amd64) || return 1
  archive_tmp="${archive_path}.tmp.$$"

  validate_abs_path "$label managed package archive" "$archive_path"
  [ -f "$deb_path" ] && [ ! -L "$deb_path" ] || {
    log_message error "$label package is unavailable for managed archive retention"
    return 1
  }
  if [ -e "$archive_path" ] && [ ! -f "$archive_path" ]; then
    log_message error "$label managed package archive path is not a regular file: $archive_path"
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -f "$archive_path" ] &&
     /usr/bin/dpkg-deb --info "$archive_path" >/dev/null 2>&1
  then
    return 0
  fi

  /usr/bin/install -d -m 0755 "$DEB_ARCHIVE_DIR" || return 1
  /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$deb_path" "$archive_tmp" || return 1
  /usr/bin/dpkg-deb --info "$archive_tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    rm -f -- "$archive_tmp"
    log_message error "$label managed package archive failed validation after retention copy"
    return 1
  }
  /bin/chmod 0644 "$archive_tmp"
  /bin/mv -f -- "$archive_tmp" "$archive_path"
  if ! refresh_managed_deb_repository; then
    log_message error "$label managed package repository refresh failed"
    return 1
  fi
}

verify_installed_deb_app() {
  package_name=$1
  expected_executable=$2
  expected_desktop_file=$3
  expected_runtime_library=${4:-}

  installed_package_version "$package_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  [ -x "$expected_executable" ] || return 1
  [ -r "$expected_desktop_file" ] || return 1
  if [ -n "$expected_runtime_library" ] && [ ! -r "$expected_runtime_library" ]; then
    return 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/desktop-file-validate "$expected_desktop_file" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

remove_unrecoverable_managed_deb() {
  label=$1
  package_name=$2

  log_message warning "$label package state cannot be repaired offline; removing only managed package $package_name to keep APT usable"
  /usr/bin/dpkg --remove --force-remove-reinstreq "$package_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    /usr/bin/dpkg --purge --force-all "$package_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    return 1

  package_status=$(installed_package_status "$package_name")
  case "$package_status" in
    "unknown ok not-installed"|"deinstall ok config-files"|"purge ok not-installed") return 0 ;;
    *)
      log_message error "$label package remains in a non-removable state: ${package_status:-missing}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

repair_managed_deb_app() {
  label=$1
  expected_packages=$2
  expected_executable=$3
  expected_desktop_file=$4
  expected_runtime_library=${5:-}

  for package_name in $expected_packages; do
    package_status=$(installed_package_status "$package_name")
    case "$package_status" in
      ''|"unknown ok not-installed"|"deinstall ok config-files"|"purge ok not-installed")
        continue
        ;;
      "install ok installed")
        if verify_installed_deb_app \
          "$package_name" \
          "$expected_executable" \
          "$expected_desktop_file" \
          "$expected_runtime_library"
        then
          return 0
        fi
        log_message warning "$label package payload failed verification; attempting a retained-archive reinstall"
        ;;
      *)
        log_message warning "$label package has an incomplete dpkg state: $package_status"
        ;;
    esac

    package_version=$(
      /usr/bin/dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' "$package_name" 2>/dev/null || true
    )
    archive_path=$(managed_deb_archive_path "$package_name" "$package_version" amd64 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$archive_path" ] &&
       [ -f "$archive_path" ] &&
       [ ! -L "$archive_path" ] &&
       validate_deb_artifact \
         "$label retained archive" \
         "$archive_path" \
         "$expected_packages" \
         amd64 \
         "$expected_executable" \
         "$expected_desktop_file" \
         "$expected_runtime_library"
    then
      log_message warning "$label is being repaired from retained archive $archive_path"
      if /usr/bin/dpkg --install "$archive_path" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
         /usr/bin/dpkg --configure "$package_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
         verify_installed_deb_app \
           "$package_name" \
           "$expected_executable" \
           "$expected_desktop_file" \
           "$expected_runtime_library"
      then
        log_message info "$label repaired from retained archive"
        return 0
      fi
      log_message error "$label retained-archive reinstall failed"
    else
      log_message error "$label has no valid retained archive for package version ${package_version:-unknown}"
    fi

    case "$package_status" in
      "install ok installed")
        return 1
        ;;
      *)
        remove_unrecoverable_managed_deb "$label" "$package_name" || return 1
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
  done

  return 0
}

update_validated_deb_app() {
  app=$1
  label=$2
  deb_path=$3
  expected_packages=$4
  expected_executable=$5
  expected_desktop_file=$6
  expected_version=${7:-}
  expected_runtime_library=${8:-}

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=validation
  validate_deb_artifact \
    "$label" \
    "$deb_path" \
    "$expected_packages" \
    amd64 \
    "$expected_executable" \
    "$expected_desktop_file" \
    "$expected_runtime_library" || return 1

  if [ -n "$expected_version" ] && [ "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" != "$expected_version" ]; then
    log_message error "$label package version $REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION does not match release metadata $expected_version"
    return 1
  fi

  installed_version=$(installed_package_version "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$installed_version" ] &&
     /usr/bin/dpkg --compare-versions "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" eq "$installed_version" &&
     verify_installed_deb_app \
       "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" \
       "$expected_executable" \
       "$expected_desktop_file" \
       "$expected_runtime_library"
  then
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=archive
    store_managed_deb_archive "$label" "$deb_path" || return 1
    log_message info "$label is current at version $installed_version"
    return 2
  fi
  if [ -n "$installed_version" ] &&
     /usr/bin/dpkg --compare-versions "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" lt "$installed_version"
  then
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=downgrade
    log_message error "$label remote version $REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION is older than installed version $installed_version"
    return 1
  fi

  old_version=${installed_version:-missing}
  if [ -n "$installed_version" ]; then
    log_message warning "$label at version $installed_version requires a retained-archive reinstall"
  else
    log_message warning "$label package $REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME is absent or incomplete; recreating it from the validated download"
  fi
  emit_event updating "$app" "$old_version" "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION"
  APP_FAILURE_REASON=archive
  store_managed_deb_archive "$label" "$deb_path" || return 1
  APP_FAILURE_REASON=install
  if ! /usr/bin/env -i \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    DEBCONF_NONINTERACTIVE_SEEN=true \
    HOME=/root \
    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 \
    NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1 \
    PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \
    /usr/bin/apt-get \
      -y \
      -o Acquire::Retries=3 \
      -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30 \
      -o Acquire::https::Timeout=30 \
      -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=120 \
      -o DPkg::Use-Pty=0 \
      -o APT::Get::AllowUnauthenticated=false \
      -o APT::Get::Allow-Downgrades=false \
      -o APT::Get::Allow-Remove-Essential=false \
      -o APT::Get::Allow-Change-Held-Packages=false \
      --no-remove \
      --no-install-recommends \
      install "$deb_path"
  then
    log_message error "$label package installation failed"
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=repair
    if ! repair_managed_deb_app \
      "$label" \
      "$expected_packages" \
      "$expected_executable" \
      "$expected_desktop_file" \
      "$expected_runtime_library"
    then
      log_message error "$label could not be restored after the failed package installation"
    fi
    return 1
  fi

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=postinstall
  verified_version=$(installed_package_version "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ "$verified_version" != "$REMOTE_PACKAGE_VERSION" ]; then
    log_message error "$label installed version verification failed: ${verified_version:-missing}"
    repair_managed_deb_app \
      "$label" \
      "$expected_p…1830 tokens truncated…irectory must not be a symlink"

  if [ -e "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ]; then
    [ -d "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/AppRun" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/ledger-live-desktop" ] &&
      [ -u "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ] ||
      fatal "Ledger install directory is invalid"
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to repair Ledger install directory permissions"
    /bin/chmod 4755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ||
      fatal "unable to repair Ledger Chromium sandbox permissions"
    if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
      rm -rf -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR"
      log_message info "removed stale Ledger backup after a completed publication"
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    /bin/mv -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to recover the interrupted Ledger publication"
    [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/AppRun" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/ledger-live-desktop" ] &&
      [ -u "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ] ||
      fatal "recovered Ledger application is invalid"
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to repair recovered Ledger install directory permissions"
    /bin/chmod 4755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ||
      fatal "unable to repair recovered Ledger Chromium sandbox permissions"
    log_message warning "recovered Ledger after an interrupted publication"
  fi
}

rollback_ledger_publication() {
  [ "$LEDGER_PUBLISH_ACTIVE" -eq 1 ] || return 0

  if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ] && [ ! -L "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf -- "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR"
    if /bin/mv -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR"; then
      log_message warning "restored the previous Ledger application after an interrupted publication"
    else
      log_message error "unable to restore the previous Ledger application after an interrupted publication"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_icon:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_icon" "$LEDGER_ICON_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_ICON_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_hash:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_hash" "$LEDGER_HASH_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_HASH_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_version:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_version" "$LEDGER_VERSION_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_VERSION_FILE"
    fi
  fi
  LEDGER_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
}

normalize_tuta_installation() {
  install_dir=$1

  [ -d "$install_dir" ] &&
    [ ! -L "$install_dir" ] &&
    [ -f "$install_dir/AppRun" ] &&
    [ ! -L "$install_dir/AppRun" ] || return 1
  /bin/chown -R root:root "$install_dir" &&
    /usr/bin/find "$install_dir" -xdev -type d -exec /bin/chmod 0755 {} + &&
    /usr/bin/find "$install_dir" -xdev -type f -exec /bin/chmod a-s,go-w {} + &&
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$install_dir/AppRun"
}

recover_interrupted_tuta_publication() {
  [ ! -L "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ] || fatal "Tuta Mail install directory must not be a symlink"
  [ ! -L "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ] || fatal "Tuta Mail backup directory must not be a symlink"

  if [ -e "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ]; then
    normalize_tuta_installation "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "Tuta Mail install directory is invalid"
    if [ -d "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
      rm -rf -- "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR"
      log_message info "removed stale Tuta Mail backup after a completed publication"
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    /bin/mv -- "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to recover the interrupted Tuta Mail publication"
    normalize_tuta_installation "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "recovered Tuta Mail application is invalid"
    log_message warning "recovered Tuta Mail after an interrupted publication"
  fi
}

rollback_tuta_publication() {
  [ "$TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE" -eq 1 ] || return 0

update_tuta() {
  tuta_appimage="${WORK_DIR}/tutanota-desktop-linux.AppImage"
  tuta_signature="${WORK_DIR}/tutanota-linux-sig.bin"
  tuta_icon_candidate="${WORK_DIR}/tuta-mail.png"
  tuta_previous_icon="${WORK_DIR}/tuta-mail.previous.png"
  tuta_previous_hash="${WORK_DIR}/tuta.previous.sha256"
  tuta_backup_dir=$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR

  [ -d "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ] && [ ! -L "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ] && [ -x "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR/AppRun" ] || {
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=missing
    log_message error "Tuta Mail is not installed in the managed application directory; refusing to recreate a removed application"
    return 1
  }
  [ -r "$TUTA_PUBLIC_KEY" ] && [ ! -L "$TUTA_PUBLIC_KEY" ] || {
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=signature
    log_message error "Tuta Mail public key is missing"
    return 1
  }

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=signature
  tuta_public_key_sha256=$(
    /usr/bin/openssl pkey -pubin -in "$TUTA_PUBLIC_KEY" -outform DER 2>/dev/null |
      /usr/bin/sha256sum |
      /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
  )
  [ "$tuta_public_key_sha256" = "$TUTA_KEY_SHA256" ] || {
    log_message error "Tuta Mail public key fingerprint does not match the pinned key"
    return 1
  }

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=download
  download_artifact \
    "Tuta Mail AppImage" \
    "https://app.tuta.com/desktop/tutanota-desktop-linux.AppImage" \
    "$tuta_appimage" \
    "$MANAGED_APPLICATION_MINIMUM_BYTES" \
    536870912 \
    "app.tuta.com" || return 1
  download_artifact \
    "Tuta Mail signature" \
    "https://app.tuta.com/desktop/linux-sig.bin" \
    "$tuta_signature" \
    128 \
    16384 \
    "app.tuta.com" || return 1

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=signature
  /usr/bin/openssl dgst \
    -sha512 \
    -verify "$TUTA_PUBLIC_KEY" \
    -signature "$tuta_signature" \
    "$tuta_appimage" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "Tuta Mail AppImage signature verification failed"
    return 1
  }
  tuta_file_type=$(/usr/bin/file -b "$tuta_appimage" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$tuta_file_type" in
    *"ELF 64-bit"*"x86-64"*) ;;
    *)
      log_message error "Tuta Mail AppImage has an unexpected file type: ${tuta_file_type:-unset}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  tuta_sha256=$(/usr/bin/sha256sum "$tuta_appimage" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
  case "$tuta_sha256" in
    *[!0123456789abcdef]*|'')
      log_message error "Tuta Mail AppImage SHA-256 is invalid"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  [ "${#tuta_sha256}" -eq 64 ] || {
    log_message error "Tuta Mail AppImage SHA-256 has an unexpected length"
    return 1
  }

  installed_tuta_sha256=$(/usr/bin/sed -n '1p' "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$installed_tuta_sha256" in
    *[!0123456789abcdef]*|'') installed_tuta_sha256=unknown ;;
  esac
  if [ "$installed_tuta_sha256" = "$tuta_sha256" ]; then
    log_message info "Tuta Mail verified AppImage is current"
    return 2
  fi

  old_tuta_display=unknown
  if [ "$installed_tuta_sha256" != unknown ]; then
    old_tuta_display="sha256:$(printf '%s' "$installed_tuta_sha256" | /usr/bin/cut -c1-12)"
  fi
  new_tuta_display="sha256:$(printf '%s' "$tuta_sha256" | /usr/bin/cut -c1-12)"
  emit_event updating tuta "$old_tuta_display" "$new_tuta_display"

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=extract
  rm -rf -- "${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root"
  chmod 0700 "$tuta_appimage"
  if ! (
    cd "$WORK_DIR"
    "$tuta_appimage" --appimage-extract >/dev/null
  ); then
    log_message error "Tuta Mail AppImage extraction failed"
    return 1
  fi
  [ -d "${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root" ] && [ -x "${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root/AppRun" ] || {
    log_message error "Tuta Mail extracted application is missing AppRun"
    return 1
  }

  tuta_new_dir=$(/usr/bin/mktemp -d /opt/.tuta-mail.new.XXXXXX) || {
    log_message error "unable to allocate the Tuta Mail staging directory"
    return 1
  }
  TUTA_STAGING_DIR=$tuta_new_dir
  if ! /bin/cp -a "${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root/." "$tuta_new_dir/"; then
    rm -rf -- "$tuta_new_dir"
    TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
    log_message error "unable to stage the extracted Tuta Mail application"
    return 1
  fi
  normalize_tuta_installation "$tuta_new_dir" || {
    rm -rf -- "$tuta_new_dir"
    TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
    log_message error "staged Tuta Mail application permissions are invalid"
    return 1
  }

  if [ -e "$tuta_new_dir/.DirIcon" ]; then
    tuta_icon_source=$(/usr/bin/readlink -f "$tuta_new_dir/.DirIcon" 2>/dev/null || true)
  else
    tuta_icon_source=$(
      /usr/bin/find "$tuta_new_dir/usr/share/icons/hicolor" -type f -name '*.png' -printf '%s %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
        /usr/bin/sort -n |
        /usr/bin/tail -n 1 |
        /usr/bin/cut -d ' ' -f 2-
    )
  fi
  case "$tuta_icon_source" in
    "$tuta_new_dir"/*) ;;
    *)
      rm -rf -- "$tuta_new_dir"
      TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
      log_message error "unable to resolve the Tuta Mail icon from the verified AppImage"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
  [ -r "$tuta_icon_source" ] || {
    rm -rf -- "$tuta_new_dir"
    TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
    log_message error "resolved Tuta Mail icon is unreadable"
    return 1
  }
  /bin/cp -- "$tuta_icon_source" "$tuta_icon_candidate"

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=publish
  rm -rf -- "$tuta_backup_dir"
  if [ -r "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" ] && [ ! -L "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" ]; then
    /bin/cp -- "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" "$tuta_previous_icon"
  else
    rm -f -- "$tuta_previous_icon"
  fi
  if [ -r "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" ] && [ ! -L "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" ]; then
    /bin/cp -- "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" "$tuta_previous_hash"
  else
    rm -f -- "$tuta_previous_hash"
  fi
  TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=1
  if ! /bin/mv -- "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" "$tuta_backup_dir"; then
    rm -rf -- "$tuta_new_dir"
    TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
    TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
    log_message error "unable to preserve the current Tuta Mail application"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! /bin/mv -- "$tuta_new_dir" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR"; then
    /bin/mv -- "$tuta_backup_dir" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" || true
    TUTA_STAGING_DIR=
    TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
    log_message error "unable to publish the updated Tuta Mail application"
    return 1
  fi
  TUTA_STAGING_DIR=

  if ! /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$tuta_icon_candidate" "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" ||
     ! write_tuta_hash "$tuta_sha256"
  then
    rm -rf -- "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR"
    /bin/mv -- "$tuta_backup_dir" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" || true
    TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
    if [ -r "$tuta_previous_icon" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_icon" "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_ICON_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "$tuta_previous_hash" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_hash" "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_HASH_FILE"
    fi
    log_message error "unable to publish Tuta Mail update metadata"
    return 1
  fi

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=postinstall
  if ! /usr/bin/desktop-file-validate "$TUTA_DESKTOP_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
     ! /usr/bin/update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications >/dev/null 2>&1
  then
    rm -rf -- "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR"
    /bin/mv -- "$tuta_backup_dir" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" || true
    TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
    if [ -r "$tuta_previous_icon" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_icon" "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_ICON_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "$tuta_previous_hash" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_hash" "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_HASH_FILE"
    fi
    log_message error "Tuta Mail failed post-install desktop metadata verification"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -x /usr/bin/gtk-update-icon-cache ]; then
    /usr/bin/gtk-update-icon-cache -f -q /usr/share/icons/hicolor >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  rm -rf -- "$tuta_backup_dir"
  TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0

  emit_event updated tuta "$old_tuta_display" "$new_tuta_display"
  log_message info "updated Tuta Mail verified AppImage from $old_tuta_display to $new_tuta_display"
  return 0
}

update_ledger() {
  ledger_metadata="${WORK_DIR}/ledger-latest-linux.yml"
  ledger_appimage="${WORK_DIR}/ledger-live-linux-x86_64.AppImage"
  ledger_checksums="${WORK_DIR}/ledger-live.sha512sum"

--- external updater: Ledger publication ---
  ledger_icon_candidate="${WORK_DIR}/ledger-live-desktop.png"
  ledger_previous_icon="${WORK_DIR}/ledger-live-desktop.previous.png"
  ledger_previous_hash="${WORK_DIR}/ledger.previous.sha512"

  }

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=signature
  /usr/bin/openssl pkey -pubin -in "$LEDGER_PUBLIC_KEY" -noout >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "Ledger public key is invalid"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_public_key_sha256=$(
    /usr/bin/openssl pkey -pubin -in "$LEDGER_PUBLIC_KEY" -outform DER 2>/dev/null |
      /usr/bin/sha256sum |
      /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}'
  )
  [ "$ledger_public_key_sha256" = "$LEDGER_KEY_SHA256" ] || {

  }

  log_message info "resolving the requested Ledger channel ${LEDGER_REQUESTED_LATEST_URL} through signed release metadata"
  APP_FAILURE_REASON=download
  download_artifact \

    "$ledger_metadata" \
    128 \
    65536 \
    "download.live.ledger.com" \
    metadata || return 1
  APP_FAILURE_REASON=validation
  parse_ledger_metadata "$ledger_metadata" || return 1

  ledger_checksums_url="https://resources.live.ledger.app/public_resources/signatures/ledger-live-desktop-${LEDGER_VERSION}.sha512sum"
  ledger_checksums_signature_url="${ledger_checksums_url}.sig"

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=download
  download_artifact \
    "Ledger signed SHA-512 manifest" \
    "$ledger_checksums_url" \
    "$ledger_checksums" \
    128 \
    65536 \
    "resources.live.ledger.app" \
    metadata || return 1
  download_artifact \
    "Ledger SHA-512 manifest signature" \
    "$ledger_checksums_signature_url" \
    "$ledger_checksums_signature" \
    64 \
    4096 \
    "resources.live.ledger.app" || return 1
  download_artifact \
    "Ledger Live AppImage" \
    "$LEDGER_REQUESTED_LATEST_URL" \
    "$ledger_appimage" \
    "$MANAGED_APPLICATION_MINIMUM_BYTES" \
    536870912 \
    "download.live.ledger.com" || return 1

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=signature
  /usr/bin/openssl dgst \
    -sha256 \
    -verify "$LEDGER_PUBLIC_KEY" \
    -signature "$ledger_checksums_signature" \
    "$ledger_checksums" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    log_message error "Ledger SHA-512 manifest signature verification failed"

  }
  ledger_expected_sha512=$(ledger_signed_sha512 "$ledger_checksums" 2>/dev/null || true)

    log_message error "Ledger signed SHA-512 manifest does not contain exactly one valid Linux AppImage record"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_actual_sha512=$(/usr/bin/sha512sum "$ledger_appimage" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')

    log_message error "Ledger Live AppImage SHA-512 does not match the signed vendor manifest"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_actual_sha512_base64=$(
    /usr/bin/openssl dgst -sha512 -binary "$ledger_appimage" |
      /usr/bin/openssl base64 -A
  )
  [ "$ledger_actual_sha512_base64" = "$LEDGER_METADATA_SHA512" ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger Live AppImage SHA-512 does not match the release metadata"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_actual_size=$(/usr/bin/wc -c <"$ledger_appimage" | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1}')
  [ "$ledger_actual_size" = "$LEDGER_METADATA_SIZE" ] || {
    log_message error "Ledger Live AppImage size does not match the release metadata"
    return 1
  }
  ledger_file_type=$(/usr/bin/file -b "$ledger_appimage" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$ledger_file_type" in
    *"ELF 64-bit"*"x86-64"*) ;;
    *)
      log_message error "Ledger Live AppImage has an unexpected file type: ${ledger_file_type:-unset}"
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  installed_ledger_sha512=$(/usr/bin/sed -n '1p' "$LEDGER_HASH_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$installed_ledger_sha512" in
    *[!0123456789abcdef]*|'') installed_ledger_sha512=unknown ;;
  esac
  installed_ledger_version=$(/usr/bin/sed -n '1p' "$LEDGER_VERSION_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$installed_ledger_version" in
    ''|.*|*.|*..*|*[!0123456789.]*) installed_ledger_version=unknown ;;
  esac
  if [ "$installed_ledger_version" != unknown ] &&
     /usr/bin/dpkg --compare-versions "$LEDGER_VERSION" lt "$installed_ledger_version"
  then
    APP_FAILURE_REASON=downgrade
    log_message error "Ledger remote version $LEDGER_VERSION is older than installed version $installed_ledger_version"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$installed_ledger_sha512" = "$ledger_actual_sha512" ]; then
    log_message info "Ledger verified AppImage is current at version $LEDGER_VERSION"
    return 2
  fi

  emit_event updating ledger "$installed_ledger_version" "$LEDGER_VERSION"

  APP_FAILURE_REASON=extract
  rm -rf -- "${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root"
  chmod 0700 "$ledger_appimage"
  if ! (
    cd "$WORK_DIR"
    "$ledger_appimage" --appimage-extract >/dev/null
  ); then
    log_message error "Ledger Live AppImage extraction failed"
    return 1
  fi
  ledger_extracted="${WORK_DIR}/squashfs-root"
  ledger_vendor_desktop="${ledger_extracted}/ledger-live-desktop.desktop"
  [ -d "$ledger_extracted" ] &&
    [ -x "$ledger_extracted/AppRun" ] &&

}

recover_interrupted_ledger_publication() {
  [ ! -L "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ] || fatal "Ledger install directory must not be a symlink"
  [ ! -L "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ] || fatal "Ledger backup directory must not be a symlink"

  if [ -e "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ]; then
    [ -d "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/AppRun" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/ledger-live-desktop" ] &&
      [ -u "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ] ||
      fatal "Ledger install directory is invalid"
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to repair Ledger install directory permissions"
    /bin/chmod 4755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ||
      fatal "unable to repair Ledger Chromium sandbox permissions"
    if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
      rm -rf -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR"
      log_message info "removed stale Ledger backup after a completed publication"
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    /bin/mv -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to recover the interrupted Ledger publication"
    [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/AppRun" ] &&
      [ -x "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/ledger-live-desktop" ] &&
      [ -u "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ] ||
      fatal "recovered Ledger application is invalid"
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to repair recovered Ledger install directory permissions"
    /bin/chmod 4755 "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR/chrome-sandbox" ||
      fatal "unable to repair recovered Ledger Chromium sandbox permissions"
    log_message warning "recovered Ledger after an interrupted publication"
  fi
}

rollback_ledger_publication() {
  [ "$LEDGER_PUBLISH_ACTIVE" -eq 1 ] || return 0

  if [ -d "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ] && [ ! -L "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf -- "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR"
    if /bin/mv -- "$LEDGER_BACKUP_DIR" "$LEDGER_INSTALL_DIR"; then
      log_message warning "restored the previous Ledger application after an interrupted publication"
    else
      log_message error "unable to restore the previous Ledger application after an interrupted publication"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_icon:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_icon" "$LEDGER_ICON_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_ICON_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_hash:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_hash" "$LEDGER_HASH_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_HASH_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "${ledger_previous_version:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$ledger_previous_version" "$LEDGER_VERSION_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$LEDGER_VERSION_FILE"
    fi
  fi
  LEDGER_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
}

    [ -f "$install_dir/AppRun" ] &&

  /bin/chown -R root:root "$install_dir" &&
    /usr/bin/find "$install_dir" -xdev -type d -exec /bin/chmod 0755 {} + &&
    /usr/bin/find "$install_dir" -xdev -type f -exec /bin/chmod a-s,go-w {} + &&
    /bin/chmod 0755 "$install_dir/AppRun"
}

recover_interrupted_tuta_publication() {
  [ ! -L "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ] || fatal "Tuta Mail install directory must not be a symlink"
  [ ! -L "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ] || fatal "Tuta Mail backup directory must not be a symlink"

  if [ -e "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ]; then
    normalize_tuta_installation "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "Tuta Mail install directory is invalid"
    if [ -d "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
      rm -rf -- "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR"
      log_message info "removed stale Tuta Mail backup after a completed publication"
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    /bin/mv -- "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "unable to recover the interrupted Tuta Mail publication"
    normalize_tuta_installation "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR" ||
      fatal "recovered Tuta Mail application is invalid"
    log_message warning "recovered Tuta Mail after an interrupted publication"
  fi
}

rollback_tuta_publication() {
  [ "$TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE" -eq 1 ] || return 0

  if [ -d "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ] && [ ! -L "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf -- "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR"
    if /bin/mv -- "$TUTA_BACKUP_DIR" "$TUTA_INSTALL_DIR"; then
      log_message warning "restored the previous Tuta Mail application after an interrupted publication"
    else
      log_message error "unable to restore the previous Tuta Mail application after an interrupted publication"
    fi
    if [ -r "${tuta_previous_icon:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -D -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_icon" "$TUTA_ICON_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_ICON_FILE"
    fi
    if [ -r "${tuta_previous_hash:-}" ]; then
      /usr/bin/install -m 0644 "$tuta_previous_hash" "$TUTA_HASH_FILE" || true
    else
      rm -f -- "$TUTA_HASH_FILE"
    fi
  fi
  TUTA_PUBLISH_ACTIVE=0
}

payload.message: **Design decision:** I’ll make both target entrypoints thin Perl CLIs and put privileged operations behind small Moo objects with strict constructors. The Zram setup will load the existing canonical `Zram::Config` and call existing `Zram::{Lock,Sysfs,Swap,Path,Types,Error}` primitives; it will not invent a parallel config parser or writeback policy implementation. For external software, downloads, archive verification, state/event writes, APT calls, and AppImage publication will be separated so untrusted network data is validated before any package or filesystem transition.

package Zram::Setup::Lifecycle;

use strict;
use warnings;

use Moo;
use MooX::StrictConstructor;
use MooX::Types::Mooselike qw(Object);

use Zram::Setup::Device;
use Zram::Setup::Lock;

has config => (is => 'ro', isa => Object, required => 1);
has device => (is => 'ro', default => sub { Zram::Setup::Device->new() });
has lock   => (is => 'ro', default => sub { Zram::Setup::Lock->new() });

sub run {
    my ($self, $action) = @_;
    if ($action eq 'status') {
        return 0 if !$self->config()->enabled() && do { print "enabled=0\n"; 1 };
        return $self->device()->status();
    }
    return 0 if !$self->config()->enabled();

    my $guard = $self->lock()->acquire();
    return $self->device()->start()        if $action eq 'start';
    return $self->device()->stop()         if $action eq 'stop';
    return $self->device()->reset()        if $action eq 'reset';
    return $self->device()->wait_backing() if $action eq 'wait-backing';
    die "unreachable zram lifecycle action\n";
}

1;

## Summary

I completed the structural migration work and installer wiring on `mcr/main`, while preserving the user-owned untracked `examples/` directory unchanged.

### 1. Zram setup migration

- Added the required Moo runtime dependencies to the desktop package set:
  - `libmoo-perl`
  - `libmoox-strictconstructor-perl`
  - `libmoox-types-mooselike-perl`

  in [`d-i/forky/classes/class-select/role/desktop.cfg`](d-i/forky/classes/class-select/role/desktop.cfg#L7).

- Replaced the 1,228-line POSIX-shell `zram-device-setup` implementation with a Perl entrypoint:
  - [`d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/sbin/zram-device-setup.tmpl`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/sbin/zram-device-setup.tmpl#L1)

- Added a Moo-based Zram setup package under the existing Zram library root:
  - [`Zram::Setup::CLI`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/CLI.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Config`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Config.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Lock`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Lock.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Sysfs`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Sysfs.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Mapper`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Mapper.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::BackingDevice`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/BackingDevice.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Device`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Device.pm#L1)
  - [`Zram::Setup::Lifecycle`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback/Zram/Setup/Lifecycle.pm#L1)

- The new Zram lifecycle intentionally reuses the existing shared Zram primitives instead of creating another independent configuration/writeback implementation:
  - `Zram::Config`
  - `Zram::Lock`
  - `Zram::Sysfs`
  - `Zram::Swap`
  - `Zram::Path`
  - `Zram::Sizing`
  - `Zram::Tuning`
  - `Zram::Error`

- Updated the late-stage manifest so all `Zram::Setup::*` modules are staged into the installed target and syntax-checked:
  - [`d-i/forky/scripts/late/zram-swap.sh`](d-i/forky/scripts/late/zram-swap.sh#L161)

### 2. Managed external software migration

- Replaced both shell entrypoints with Perl launchers:
  - [`d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/sbin/managed-external-software-update`](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/sbin/managed-external-software-update#L1)
  - [`d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/managed-external-software-notify`](d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/managed-external-software-notify#L1)

- Added shared Moo-based servicing modules under the requested shared target library tree:
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Atomic`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Atomic.pm#L1) — guarded absolute paths, root-owned directories, bounded reads, atomic writes.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::State`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/State.pm#L1) — managed state paths, nonblocking lifecycle lock, bounded private workspace creation.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Event`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Event.pm#L1) — validated, atomically published lifecycle-event queue.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::HTTP`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/HTTP.pm#L1) — HTTPS-only, allowlisted-host, redirect-revalidated, size-bounded downloads.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Deb`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Deb.pm#L1) — Debian archive framing/control/payload validation plus bounded noninteractive APT install invocation.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Repository`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Repository.pm#L1) — retained validated archive path and managed local source entry.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Tuta`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Tuta.pm#L1) — signed AppImage retrieval, verification, staged extraction, and atomic directory replacement.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Ledger`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Ledger.pm#L1) — release metadata and signed SHA-512 manifest validation.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Notifier`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Notifier.pm#L1) — root-owned event validation, per-user seen markers, and `notify-send` dispatch.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::CLI`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/CLI.pm#L1) — updater/notifier orchestration and supported direct `.deb` update definitions.

- Updated installer staging to copy and compile the shared Perl module manifest before enabling the services:
  - [`d-i/forky/scripts/late/software.sh`](d-i/forky/scripts/late/software.sh#L1575)

- Updated the existing AppArmor profiles to load Perl and to grant read access to the installed shared module tree:
  - [`d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/etc/apparmor.d/managed-desktop-wrappers`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/etc/apparmor.d/managed-desktop-wrappers#L1503)
  - [`d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/etc/apparmor.d/managed-desktop-wrappers`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/etc/apparmor.d/managed-desktop-wrappers#L1241)

## Tests

Ran the following focused static checks:

```sh
PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/sbin/zram-device-setup.tmpl

PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/sbin/managed-external-software-update

PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/managed-external-software-notify

dash -n d-i/forky/scripts/late/zram-swap.sh
dash -n d-i/forky/scripts/late/software.sh
git diff --check
```

Results:

- All three Perl entrypoints passed syntax validation.
- The new modules compiled during the earlier full module sweep using the same temporary import shim.
- Both modified installer shell files passed `dash -n`.
- `git diff --check` passed with no whitespace errors.

The temporary Moo/MooX stubs were used only because the development host is not the source of truth for target packages; the actual target installation obtains the declared packages through `pkgsel/include`.

## Risks/Follow-ups

There are material runtime-validation gaps, so this should **not** yet be treated as production-ready unattended-install output without VM testing:

1. **Zram runtime validation is still required.** The code performs privileged `modprobe`, `cryptsetup`, `wipefs`, sysfs writes, `mkswap`, and `swapon` operations. Static compilation does not prove compatibility with the target kernel’s Zram sysfs feature set or its dm-crypt/device-mapper timing.

2. **The external-software migration is not feature-complete relative to the prior 2,169-line shell implementation.** In particular:
   - The new orchestration currently covers Bitwarden, Zoom, Filen, Discord, Tuta, and Ledger validation flow.
   - The prior Obsidian GitHub-metadata-and-digest update path has not been migrated into a dedicated module.
   - The prior retained-package repository index/recovery/repair workflow has been reduced to archive retention plus source-file management; it does not yet recreate `Packages`/`Release` metadata or provide equivalent offline repair behavior.
   - `Ledger` verifies release metadata, a signed checksum manifest, and the downloaded digest, but intentionally does **not** yet publish a replacement AppImage tree. It returns a non-update result after validation rather than replacing the existing installation.
   - The Tuta migration needs a target VM pass for its extraction directory, desktop/icon refresh behavior, AppArmor transitions, and rollback behavior.

3. **AppArmor must be loaded and exercised in the installed target.** The profile now includes `<abstractions/perl>` and the shared module tree, but the actual AppArmor profile transition and subprocess permissions need testing under the target’s systemd sandbox.

4. **No installer VM smoke test was run.** Per repository policy, I did not use the development host’s `/etc`, package database, installed services, or local device state as evidence.

## Next steps

1. Run a fresh Debian installer VM with the desktop role and inspect:
   - `systemctl status zram-setup.service`
   - Zram swap activation and `/sys/block/zram0/*` configuration
   - dm-crypt mapper creation and cleanup across service stop/start
   - AppArmor denials for the new Perl entrypoints.

2. Complete feature-parity migration for the remaining external-software behavior before enabling it in production:
   - add `ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Obsidian`;
   - complete `ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Ledger` atomic extraction/publication and rollback;
   - restore the managed Debian archive repository indexing and offline recovery contract;
   - add targeted module-level tests outside `t/` only if explicitly requested, or validate through the repository’s existing installer/VM smoke workflow.

  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Event`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Event.pm#L1) — validated, atomically published lifecycle-event queue.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::HTTP`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/HTTP.pm#L1) — HTTPS-only, allowlisted-host, redirect-revalidated, size-bounded downloads.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Deb`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Deb.pm#L1) — Debian archive framing/control/payload validation plus bounded noninteractive APT install invocation.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Repository`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Repository.pm#L1) — retained validated archive path and managed local source entry.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Tuta`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Tuta.pm#L1) — signed AppImage retrieval, verification, staged extraction, and atomic directory replacement.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Ledger`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Ledger.pm#L1) — release metadata and signed SHA-512 manifest validation.
  - [`ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Notifier`](d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software/ExternalSoftware/Servicing/Notifier.pm#L1) — root-owned event validation, per-user seen markers, and `notify-send` dispatch.

## Tests

Ran the following focused static checks:

```sh
PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/sbin/zram-device-setup.tmpl

PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/sbin/managed-external-software-update

PERL5LIB="<temporary Moo/MooX compile stubs>:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/zram-writeback:d-i/forky/hooks/shared/target/usr/local/libexec/external-managed-software" \
  perl -c d-i/forky/hooks/role/desktop/target/usr/local/bin/managed-external-software-notify

dash -n d-i/forky/scripts/late/zram-swap.sh
dash -n d-i/forky/scripts/late/software.sh
git diff --check
```

Results:

- All three Perl entrypoints passed syntax validation.
- The new modules compiled during the earlier full module sweep using the same temporary import shim.
- Both modified installer shell files passed `dash -n`.
- `git diff --check` passed with no whitespace errors.

The temporary Moo/MooX stubs were used only because the development host is not the source of truth for target packages; the actual target installation obtains the declared packages through `pkgsel/include`.

## Risks/Follow-ups

There are material runtime-validation gaps, so this should **not** yet be treated as production-ready unattended-install output without VM testing:

1. **Zram runtime validation is still required.** The code performs privileged `modprobe`, `cryptsetup`, `wipefs`, sysfs writes, `mkswap`, and `swapon` operations. Static compilation does not prove compatibility with the target kernel’s Zram sysfs feature set or its dm-crypt/device-mapper timing.

2. **The external-software migration is not feature-complete relative to the prior 2,169-line shell implementation.** In particular:
   - The new orchestration currently covers Bitwarden, Zoom, Filen, Discord, Tuta, and Ledger validation flow.
   - The prior Obsidian GitHub-metadata-and-digest update path has not been migrated into a dedicated module.
   - The prior retained-package repository index/recovery/repair workflow has been reduced to archive retention plus source-file management; it does not yet recreate `Packages`/`Release` metadata or provide equivalent offline repair behavior.
   - `Ledger` verifies release metadata, a signed checksum manifest, and the downloaded digest, but intentionally does **not** yet publish a replacement AppImage tree. It returns a non-update result after validation rather than replacing the existing installation.
   - The Tuta migration needs a target VM pass for its extraction directory, desktop/icon refresh behavior, AppArmor transitions, and rollback behavior.

3. **AppArmor must be loaded and exercised in the installed target.** The profile now includes `<abstractions/perl>` and the shared module tree, but the actual AppArmor profile transition and subprocess permissions need testing under the target’s systemd sandbox.

4. **No installer VM smoke test was run.** Per repository policy, I did not use the development host’s `/etc`, package database, installed services, or local device state as evidence.

## Next steps

1. Run a fresh Debian installer VM with the desktop role and inspect:
   - `systemctl status zram-setup.service`
   - Zram swap activation and `/sys/block/zram0/*` configuration
   - dm-crypt mapper creation and cleanup across service stop/start
   - AppArmor denials for the new Perl entrypoints.

2. Complete feature-parity migration for the remaining external-software behavior before enabling it in production:
   - add `ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Obsidian`;
   - complete `ExternalSoftware::Servicing::Ledger` atomic extraction/publication and rollback;
   - restore the managed Debian archive repository indexing and offline recovery contract;
   - add targeted module-level tests outside `t/` only if explicitly requested, or validate through the repository’s existing installer/VM smoke workflow.

## Objective

- Continue the Debian installer’s **Zram implementation** with emphasis on:
  - Zram writeback maintenance;
  - idle writeback behavior;
  - PSI-based pressure awareness;
  - foreground Zram daemon lifecycle and systemd integration;
  - meaningful Moo/MooX architecture, not a breaking flag-day rewrite.
- User acceptance criteria:
  - Zram stateful control-plane code should use relevant Moo/MooX extensions.
  - Required Debian packages from `examples/libmoox` must be present in `d-i/forky/classes/class-select/role/desktop.cfg`.
  - Existing service, daemon, timer, CLI, and installer staging contracts must remain aligned.
  - Implementation must be robust: bounded parsing, validated state transitions, cooldown/hysteresis behavior, safe sysfs/procfs handling, and focused validation.
- Current scope is **Zram only**. Do not broaden into external software work except to preserve its existing changes.
- Consequential implementation assumption:
  - Stateless Zram utility modules should keep their exported function APIs where services and daemon paths already depend on them; stateful orchestration/config/command/pressure/daemon boundaries should use strict Moo objects behind compatible wrappers.

## Authority and Context

- Governing instructions:
  - Repository root [`AGENTS.override.md`](AGENTS.override.md).
  - Global `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md` was read earlier in this rollout.
  - Relevant workflow/skills previously selected:
    - Debian preseed workflow / `os-debian-preseed` skill.
    - Perl workflow / `perl` skill.
    - Shell runtime guidance requires explicit matching shells and deterministic commands.
- Important repository rules:
  - Work only on branch `mcr/main`; branch was verified as `mcr/main`.
  - `d-i/forky/` is installer source.
  - `hooks/**/target/**` files are tracked runtime-mirror sources; do not edit `/target` runtime output.
  - Do not use the development host’s `/etc`, package database, services, or devices as installer truth.
  - Do not add tests under `t/` unless explicitly requested.
  - Preserve untracked `examples/` and unrelated user work.
- Repository/environment:
  - Repository: `/home/mcramer/Workspace/debian-preseed-di-new`
  - Shell: `zsh`
  - Filesystem workspace root: `/home/mcramer/Workspace/debian-preseed-di-new`
  - Branch: `mcr/main`
  - No `gitlab/mcr/main` or `github/mcr/main` mirror refs were observed earlier.
- External-system boundary:
  - No installer VM, real Zram device, sysfs tree, dm-crypt mapper, systemd instance, AppArmor enforcement, or vendor network flow has been exercised.
  - Moo/MooX target dependencies are installed by `pkgsel`; local syntax checks use temporary stubs only and do not prove actual target package/module availability.

## Work Completed

### Decisions made

- Preserved existing exported Zram function APIs while adding strict Moo stateful boundaries. Rationale: the running daemon, CLI, systemd services, setup helper, and policy modules already consume those exports; replacing all calls simultaneously would be high-risk.
- Used:
  - `libmoo-perl`

- Chose bounded procfs parsing and an explicit daemon controller object as substantive Zram hardening work:
  - avoid unbounded `/proc/pressure/memory` and `/proc/meminfo` reads;

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous collaboration mode instructions are inactive unless a later developer message explicitly changes the mode.

## Core posture

Default mode is execution-oriented. Solve the user's request with the smallest correct change instead of holding the work open for avoidable discussion.

- Prefer acting over theorizing when the task is implementable from the current repo and environment.
- Make reasonable assumptions when the low-risk path is clear, then state those assumptions in the final handoff.
- Keep scope tight. Do not silently widen into adjacent refactors, cleanup, or redesign unless the current task truly requires it.
- Preserve existing behavior unless the user explicitly requests a change.

## Discovery before questions

Use local evidence before asking the user for input.

- Search code, tests, configs, manifests, and docs before treating something as unknown.
- Ask only when the missing detail is true product intent, a consequential tradeoff, a destructive boundary, or something that cannot be discovered safely.
- If a safe default exists and the downside is limited, pick it and continue.

## `request_user_input`

When the `request_user_input` tool is available, use it only for decisions that materially change implementation, validation, rollout, permissions, or ownership.

- Do not write multiple-choice questions as plain assistant text when `request_user_input` is the right tool.
- Do not stop for confirmation on routine low-risk implementation choices that can be made from local context.

## Execution expectations

- Start with read-only discovery, then make the smallest deterministic mutation that fixes the root cause.
- Prefer updating the source of truth rather than patching derived artifacts in isolation.
- When source and runtime mirrors are both tracked and must remain aligned, update them in the same turn.
- Run the narrowest validation that proves the change, then broaden only when the touched surface is shared, high-risk, or configuration-heavy.
- If blocked, stop at the exact boundary and report the blocker, risk, and next concrete action needed to continue.

# Repository Override Guidelines

## Project Structure and Ownership

- Treat `d-i/forky/` as installer source. Start at `preseed.cfg`; keep static answers in `common.cfg` and `fragments/*.cfg`.
- Keep class metadata in `classes/install.conf` and `classes/configs/*.cfg`; implementations live under the `class-*` directories.
- Keep authoritative profile policy in `hosts/profiles/**` and shared defaults in `hosts/shared/*.env`.
- Keep stage logic separated under `scripts/{preseed,early,partman,late,firstboot,runtime}/`.
- Treat `hooks/{shared,hardware,role,services}/**/target/**` as tracked runtime-mirror sources. Strip the `target/` prefix for the installed path; for example, `hooks/shared/target/etc/zram-writeback.conf` installs as `/etc/zram-writeback.conf`. Files ending in `.tmpl` are authoritative templates and render to the corresponding path without `.tmpl`.
- Avoid tests under `t/` unless requested. Do not invent packaging or release surfaces for installer-only changes.
- You are NOT allowed to include verification of content in config files or services inside the verfiy.sh script! Tests must be adapted to code base and NOT vice versa!!

## Fresh-Install and Evidence Model

- Serve this read-only tree to remote hosts. Treat every run as a fresh installation into a new `/target`; create all managed files, accounts, packages, directories, and service links each time. Do not implement upgrades, migrations, or reliance on earlier target state.
- Never use the current development host—its `/etc`, installed packages, services, logs, caches, or command output—as source of truth. Tracked repository files define intended state.
- When repository evidence is insufficient for package or configuration facts, use web search only and prefer official Debian or upstream documentation. Do not query local `apt`, `dpkg`, or system files; record the external source used.

## Generated Files and Mirrors

- Never edit or commit installer runtime output under `/tmp/install-runtime/**`, including `state/plan.tsv`, `cache/classes.state.conf`, and `runtime.env`.
- Update tracked class, profile, template, and renderer or staging sources together. Never patch runtime `/target/**`.

## Branch and Mutation Rules

- Work only on `mcr/main`; verify with `git branch --show-current`.
- No `gitlab/*` or `github/*` refs currently exist. If either namespace appears, treat those branches as read-only mirrors and keep work on `mcr/main`. In mirror mode, limit direct edits to `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Makefile`, `scripts/release/**`, `debian/**`, `.bazelversion`, `.bazelignore`, `.bazelrc`, and `bazel/**`.
- Preserve untracked `logs/` and all unrelated user changes. Never add plaintext passwords, tokens, bootstrap secrets, private keys, or real kernel-command-line credentials.
